brief.headline: SK Hynix PER Flips Samsung; Q1 DRAM Contracts +90–95% as HBM3E Holds 66% Mix Through 2026
brief.summary: <cite index="27-1,30-22">SK hynix's 2026 forward PER reached 6.79x, surpassing Samsung Electronics' 6.77x for the first time</cite>, driven by <cite index="27-26">SK hynix's one-month gain of 78.68% versus Samsung's 35.44%</cite>. <cite index="13-6,13-7">Q1 2026 DRAM contract prices surged 90–95% QoQ (from prior 55–60% estimate), with NAND Flash up 55–60% QoQ</cite>. <cite index="10-1,10-7">HBM3E will account for 66% of total HBM output in 2026, down from 87% in 2025</cite>, while <cite index="1-3">Samsung and SK hynix raised HBM3E prices ~20% for 2026 deliveries</cite>. <cite index="34-5,34-8">Hyperscaler 2026 capex now stands at $725 billion, nearly double mid-2025 consensus of $365 billion</cite>.
brief.pair_trade_view: Fade SK Hynix into Samsung near-term. <cite index="21-14,21-15">Forward PER parity (6.79x vs 6.77x) marks first-ever valuation crossover</cite>, ending a 2.8-point discount three months ago. <cite index="23-4,23-6,23-7">UBS raised Samsung 2027 HBM shipments to 23Gb (from 20.3Gb), forecasting market share parity with SK hynix by 2027</cite>, while trimming SK hynix 2026/27 estimates. <cite index="29-15">Samsung faces 18-day strike risk (July 21–Aug 7)</cite>, but <cite index="21-9,21-19">relative valuation and profit-take fatigue after SK hynix's 78% monthly run</cite> favor rotation. Samsung @ 284k won trades 6.77x '26E EPS; SK hynix @ 1.976M won at 6.79x with heavier momentum overhang.

memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="13-1,13-6">Q1 '26 DRAM contracts revised to +90–95% QoQ from +55–60%</cite>; <cite index="13-11">PC DRAM rose over 100% QoQ</cite>. <cite index="17-2,17-3">DDR4 spot hit $2.10/Gbit, exceeding HBM3e contract at $1.70/Gbit</cite>. <cite index="11-9,11-10">Suppliers reallocating capacity to server DRAM and HBM, constraining legacy nodes</cite>. <cite index="15-1,15-18">Q2 '26 DRAM +58–63% QoQ, NAND +70–75% QoQ expected</cite>. No relief until late 2027.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="1-3">Samsung and SK hynix hiked HBM3E prices ~20% for 2026</cite>, <cite index="1-1">as both prioritize HBM4 ramp, keeping HBM3E supply tight</cite>. <cite index="6-7,6-9">HBM3E remains flagship product in 2026, accounting for ~2/3 of shipments, with HBM4 ramping in H2</cite>. <cite index="5-1,5-20">Nvidia requested 16-Hi HBM4 delivery by Q4 2026</cite>; <cite index="10-11,10-12">discussions exploratory, no contracts yet</cite>. <cite index="8-1,8-12">HBM3E ~$300/36GB stack; B200 with 8 stacks costs $2,400 in memory alone, exceeding logic die cost</cite>. <cite index="6-11,6-12">SK hynix holds 62% HBM shipments (Q2 '25), 57% revenue (Q3), with UBS expecting 70% HBM4 share for Nvidia Rubin in 2026</cite>. <cite index="23-2,23-6">UBS: Samsung to reach HBM share parity with SK hynix by 2027</cite>.

news_pulse.headline: SK hynix forward PER surpasses Samsung for first time at 6.79x vs 6.77x
news_pulse.implication: Valuation gap closed after 78% monthly rally; relative value now favors Samsung rotation as profit-taking risk rises.

news_pulse.headline: TrendForce revises Q1 '26 DRAM contract +90–95% QoQ (from +55–60%), NAND +55–60% (from +33–38%)
news_pulse.implication: Unprecedented pricing power; PC DRAM >100% QoQ as HBM/server allocation starves consumer segments. Gross margin upside for both names.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung, SK hynix raised HBM3E prices ~20% for 2026 deliveries
news_pulse.implication: Nvidia H200 China approval and hyperscaler ASIC demand keep HBM3E tight despite HBM4 entry; pricing tailwind into H2.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler 2026 capex now $725B, nearly double $365B consensus from mid-2025
news_pulse.implication: AI infrastructure spend 75% AI-related; memory demand locked in through 2027 despite supply-constrained environment.

news_pulse.headline: UBS: Samsung 2027 HBM shipments raised to 23Gb (+13% vs prior 20.3Gb); SK hynix 2026/27 trimmed
news_pulse.implication: Samsung capex pull-in closing HBM gap; competitive positioning improving into Nvidia Rubin cycle (H2 '26).

news_pulse.headline: Nvidia requested 16-Hi HBM4 delivery by Q4 2026; Samsung/SK hynix/Micron accelerating development
news_pulse.implication: Next-gen memory roadmap pulling forward; technical hurdles (bonding, thermal) remain but demand visibility strong.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS capacity at 75–80k wpm (late '25), ramping to 130k wpm by end-2026; demand CAGR 80%
news_pulse.implication: Advanced packaging remains bottleneck; Nvidia locked >60% through '26, limiting supply for hyperscaler custom ASICs.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung shares +4% intraday to 300k won as SK hynix pauses at 1.976M won after 7.68% surge prior session
news_pulse.implication: Technical consolidation after SK hynix hit 1.99M won intraday high; rotation flow into Samsung on relative valuation.

brief.derivatives_signal: KOSPI +0.93% to 7,916 (09:30 KST). <cite index="26-1,26-3">Samsung + SK hynix now 42.2% of KOSPI (May)</cite>, up from <40% in Q1. <cite index="24-7,24-8,24-9">U.S. DRAM ETF (SK hynix 25.95%, Samsung 20.27%) net assets $6.66B; weekly inflow $2.55B, 2nd-largest among U.S. equity ETFs after SPY</cite>. <cite index="24-10,24-11,24-12">REX 2X leveraged SK hynix ADR ETF filing; Korea single-stock leveraged ETFs (Samsung/SK hynix) launch May 27</cite>. Concentration risk rising; volatility likely to spike on any strike escalation or CoWoS allocation disappointment.
watch_for_next_3h: Samsung union statement / back-channel mediation update ahead of July 21 strike deadline
SK hynix price action above/below 1.95M won (support after 1.99M intraday high)
TrendForce Q2 '26 memory pricing update (due late May); any upward revision to +58–63% DRAM estimate
Nvidia/hyperscaler HBM allocation news (Samsung HBM4 Broadcom test results, Google TPU v8 ramp timing)
KOSPI derivatives flow into close (single-stock ETF arb positioning ahead of May 27 launch)
